integrity: The universal proof is exact: a continued-fraction matrix argument determines the parity of the least positive Bézout coefficient, and the source's inclusion-exclusion framework then selects the two-prime-power totient branch. Finite computation is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem resolves only the two-prime-power branch and the associated Bézout parity question. It does not give a general closed formula for the new totient on integers with three or more distinct odd prime factors. A residual literature risk is an unindexed classical formulation of the elementary continued-fraction parity identity.
title: Euclidean quotient parity resolves the two-prime totient branch
